units.translation: the entrails –, of which the father tasted
and they who held the city, thus they depart
to this man –, who – sacrificed his own child
Ruin and the Fury, by whom I slew this man
divinity, who falls upon
and the rest
the earth itself, which gives birth to all things
for they are enemies to whom it befell to mourn with hair
against the rulers, whom may I one day see dead
remember the baths in which you were stripped
remember the net with which they first ensnared you
for shame in councils does not make words blind, said the man with courage
this is the work of men, with whom we shall share
shore –, which now upon the admiral's body you lie
Orestes –, whom I reared
and you who within the house hold the wealth-rich inner chamber, hear, gods of one mind
breast, at which you often slumbering drew milk
and whom you should love, you hate
you killed whom you should not
and there came to whom is the care of secret battle, the guileful vengeance
to a man –, from whom she bore the weight of children beneath her girdle
Themis, who indeed second after her mother sat upon this oracle
ancient children, with whom no god mingles
vomiting the clots which you drew off from the murder
mother who bore me
the land –, which indeed the Achaean lords divided
Agamemnon –, with whom you made Troy, the city of Ilium, cityless
of the man, whom he killed
you heard what you heard
for no mother is there who gave me birth
of the savior, who respecting his father's fate saves me
of the house in which the thunderbolt is sealed
war –, in which there will be a terrible love of glory
for it is possible for me not to say what I do not accomplish
of whom the city, of whom the land and white water, and highest gods and heavily honored
of the marriage bed, from which right excludes
all the land, through which the holy Strymon flows
of mortals, who do not obtain lawful justice
the avenger, who not even in Hades sets free the dead
of Io, through whom we boast to be of your race
and mortals, who then were lawful possessors of the land
a hard-to-fight guardian, whom what house could have?
Zeus – who by ancient law sets destiny aright
and the gods, who hold the earth
the throne, to which watery snow becomes a cup
lest we suffer, for which much toil, and much sea was plowed by the spear
the gods who dwell around the stream of Erasinus
and the rivers, which through the land pour a peaceful drink
this is he who once hurled a missile at me
the toils, which you have drunk to the dregs
those near Zeus, of whom on the Idaean hill is the altar of ancestral Zeus
whom neither the ray of the sun looks upon
of your mother I speak, who bore you
life, which brings sorrows
of rocks –, with which then you, throwing, will easily rout the Ligurian army
from which indeed Rhegium is called
Zeus, who killed this man
a canker, which eats the flesh of my foot
a bird –, which in the appearing spring shakes its wing
of the same sow, which has done me many evils in the house
who had four yoked mares
and I will speak, having no blame for men, but explaining the goodwill I have shown
who at first seeing saw in vain
why should I fear, for whom it is not fated to die?
